newsitem.title: USA: US Airways to lay off more pilots.
newsitem.headline: US Airways to lay off more pilots.

text.p: US Airways Group Inc. said Monday it plans to lay off 42 pilots this fall as it continues to implement downsizing plans announced earlier this year.
The 42 pilots slated to lose their jobs are in addition to the 103 job cuts that were previously announced, said US Airways spokesman Rick Weintraub.
In May, US Airways said it would cut unprofitable routes, consolidate facilities and reduce its fleet.
US Airways is currently in labour talks with its unionized employees. Until a cost-cutting agreement is reached, US Airways has said, it must focus on becoming a smaller, regional carrier.
The new layoff announcement "is part of management's harsh negotiating strategy," said Jim Gardner, a spokesman for the Air Line Pilots Association, which represents 5,000 employees at the carrier.
The union said it will picket Tuesday to express support for the pilots who are scheduled to lose their jobs on July 1 as part of the first round of layoffs.
The pilots union said it recognises US Airways' competitive challenges but said management's downsizing plan "fails to position this airline for the future."
US Airways' stock lost $1 to $35 on the New York Stock Exchange.
